answer.decision: Start signing with the new key immediately while temporarily verifying both old and new keys.
answer.action: Disable the old private key for signing, activate the new signing key, and publish/load both public verification keys across all services. Retain old-key verification for at least the 45-minute access-token lifetime, then remove it after confirming old-key tokens have expired and rotation metrics are healthy; keep the overlap within the 24-hour policy limit.
reasons: This satisfies the requirement that the old key stop signing immediately while allowing already-issued access tokens to remain valid.
A verification overlap covering the 45-minute token lifetime avoids forced logout for users holding old-key access tokens.
Server-side refresh-token validation allows clients to obtain new-key access tokens without embedding or updating signing keys.
All services can load two verification keys without restarting, making dual verification operationally feasible.
Immediate replacement with new-key-only verification would invalidate outstanding tokens and could exceed the 2 percent logout limit; continuing old-key signing violates an explicit constraint.
assumptions: All token-verifying services receive both public keys before or atomically with the signing-key switch.
No old-key access tokens have validity beyond the stated 45-minute expiration.
Disabling the old private key prevents every signing path from using it.
Normal refresh behavior does not require a client-version update.
risks: Propagation lag or misconfiguration could cause temporary authentication failures in services that have not loaded the new verification key.
Removing old-key verification before all old-key access tokens expire could force logouts.
Keeping old-key verification longer than necessary increases exposure if forged old-key tokens can still be produced and must never exceed the 24-hour policy limit.
Clock skew may require a small safety margin beyond 45 minutes before removing old-key verification.

citations.claim: The old key must stop signing immediately, and signing can be disabled independently from retaining its public verification material.
Access tokens expire after 45 minutes and refresh tokens are validated server-side.
All deployed services can load two verification keys without a restart.
Policy allows verification-key overlap for up to 24 hours.
Services verify tokens using server-published public keys, so client key embedding is not a rotation dependency.
